PLIERS AND NIPPERS FOR ELECTRONICS — 

SINGLE PURPOSE PLIERS — 

SNIPE NOSE PLIERS — SPECIFICATION 



UDC 62r88r4[ 621-38]

MANAK BHAVAN, 9 BAHADUR SHAH ZAFAR MARG 
NEW DELHI 110002 

May 1993 Price Group 1 



Assembly Hand Tools Sectional Committee, PE 05 



FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Assembly Hand Tools Sectional Committee had been approved by the Production Engineering 
Division Council. 

These types of pliers are generally used for holding and gripping while working on electronic items. 
For general purpose snipe nose pliers, reference may be made to IS 5658 : 1990 *Snipe nose pliers — 
Specification'. 

While formulating this standard, considerable assistance has been taken from ISO 9655 : 1989 
Pliers and nippers for electronics — Single purpose pliers — Pliers for gripping and manipulating 
issued by International Organization for Standardization ( ISO ). 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, 
the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in 
accordance with IS 2 : I960 'Rules for rounding off the numerical values {revised)\ The number 
of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified 
value in this standard. 



IS 13766 : 1993 



Indian Standard 



PLIERS AND NIPPERS FOR ELECTRONICS — 

SINGLE PURPOSE PLIERS — 

SNIPE NOSE PLIERS — SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

This standard covers the dimensions and other 
requirements for the snipe nose pliers for use 
while working on electronic gadgets. 

2 REFERENCES 

Following Indian Standards areiiecessary adjuncts 
to this standard: 



NOTE — 
IS 13636 



For testing the hardness requirements, refer 
1992. 



IS No. 



Title 



13610 : 1992 Pliers and nippers for electronics 

— Nomenclature 

13636 : 1992 Pliers and nippers for electronics 

— Technical supply conditions 

3 NOMENCLATURE 

For the purpose of this standard, the nomencla- 
ture as given in IS 13610 : 1992 shall apply. 

4 DIMENSIONS 

The dimensions of snipe nose pliers for electronics 
shall be as given in Table 1. 

5 HARDNESS 

The hardness shall be as follows: 

Body 350 to 510 HV ( «35 to 50 HRC) 

Near Cutting 510 to 700 HV ( -50 to 60 HRC ) 
Edges 



6 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 

The material, manufacture, workmanship and 
finish, insulation tests, preservation and packing 
and sampling shall conform to IS 13636 : 1992. 

7 TESTS 

7.1 The pliers shall be tested for the requirements 
as specified in IS 13636: 1992. Load test shall 
also be carried out on the pliers as given in 
IS 13636 : 1992. The values of the load for the 
load test arc given in IS 13636 : 1992. 



8 DESIGNATION 

The snipe nose pliers for electronics 
designated by its commonly used name, 
size and number of this standard. 



shall be 
nominal 



Example: 

Snipe nose pliers for electronics and 



of 



nominal size 140 mm shall be designated as: 
Snipe Nose Plier Electronics — IS 13766 — 
140 

9 MARKING 

9.1 The pliers shall be clearly and legibly stamped 
with the nominal size, its use with electronics, 
manufacturer's name, initials or the recognized 
trade-mark. The year of manufacture may also 
be legibly stamped if required by the purchaser.

Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisioas of the Swr^aw o/ /mf/an 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the 
producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity 
to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the 
use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained 
from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious developn^cnt of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending lo connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in 
any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the 
course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade 
designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications ), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments arc issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also 
reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no 
changes arc needed; if the review indicates that changes arc needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of 
Indian Standards should ascertain that they arc in possession of the latest amendments or edition by 
referring to the latent issue of * BIS Handbook' and 'Standards Monthly Additions*. Comments on this 
Indian Standard may be sent to BIS giving the following reference: 

Doc: No. PE05 (0029)
